coursesExamined.name: Personal & Professional Development
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
coursesExamined.contribution: RequiredYear1personal/professionaldevelopment.

coursesExamined.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces financial accounting, management accounting and investment appraisal, including accounting's social role and accountability implications. Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.
coursesExamined.contribution: Financial and management accounting, costing, pricing, budgeting, control, sustainable management accounting and discounted cash-flow investment appraisal provide a substantive accounting and financial-decision foundation. This does not supply a full international accounting or tax sequence.

coursesExamined.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. AI foundations and limitations lead into applications across enterprise functions and industries, labour-market change, productivity, innovation, market structure and inequality. Governance, corporate responsibility, regulation and future scenarios connect technological developments to institutional choices. Students analyze business cases and competing scholarly arguments, then investigate a country's AI readiness, workforce, regulation and industrial policy.
coursesExamined.contribution: examines managerial, organisational and societal implications of AI and technological change

traceOverrides.rationale: examines managerial and organisational implications of AI and technological change within a broad international-business curriculum

coursesExamined.name: Transnational Business Law
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies legal frameworks governing cross-border business transactions, combining comparative and international perspectives with practical legal problem-solving. Topics include trade regulation, contracts and international sales, transport and documentary transactions, finance, services, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce. Advisory assignments assess contractual outcomes, risk allocation, intellectual-property protection and e-commerce compliance. A simulated arbitration develops written legal argument and oral advocacy.
coursesExamined.contribution: Direct contribution: transnational contracts, trade, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce address legal aspects of cross-border business; no unestablished company-law coverage is claimed.

coursesExamined.name: Money, Banking & Finance
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines financial markets and institutions, including the pricing of bonds, stocks and derivatives, interest rates and their risk and term structure, commercial-bank balance sheets and performance, financial structure and regulation, banking fragility and financial crises, central banks, money creation and monetary policy. Students apply algebraic and graphical analysis to financial and monetary problems. In the Stanford Banking Game they manage a simulated bank, analyse performance in Excel dashboards, forecast financial statements, and make evidence-based decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk. A small research project extends a selected financial or monetary research article through additional literature, a case study or updated evidence.
coursesExamined.contribution: Bond, stock and derivative pricing, interest-rate risk, bank balance sheets, regulation, fragility and monetary policy provide direct financial-market and institutional content. The simulated bank uses Excel forecasts and capital, liquidity and risk decisions. This is a specific partial finance relationship, with different coverage from RSM corporate finance.

traceOverrides.rationale: Bond, stock and derivative pricing, interest-rate risk, bank balance sheets, regulation, fragility and monetary policy provide direct financial-market and institutional content. The simulated bank uses Excel forecasts and capital, liquidity and risk decisions. This is a specific partial finance relationship, with different coverage from RSM corporate finance.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Economics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces microeconomic principles and short-run macroeconomic analysis. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides economic foundations on firms, markets, incentives and macroeconomic conditions

coursesExamined.name: International Macroeconomics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines short-, medium- and long-run macroeconomic dynamics and policy, including international dimensions. Students study goods, financial and labour markets, inflation and unemployment, economic growth, expectations and the open economy. IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models connect markets and policy effects. Algebraic and graphical analysis and interpretation of macroeconomic indicators support the evaluation of economic developments and fiscal and monetary policy.
coursesExamined.contribution: examines growth, inflation, business cycles and policy shaping the international business environment

coursesExamined.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops microeconomic theory through consumer behaviour, imperfectly competitive markets and economy-wide allocation. Students examine choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations, then monopoly, strategic behaviour and labour and capital markets. General equilibrium, efficiency, externalities and government complete the analysis. Algebraic problem-solving and graphical analysis are connected to the interpretation and evaluation of research papers.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops microeconomic and behavioural analysis of consumer and firm decisions

traceOverrides.rationale: develops microeconomic and behavioural analysis of consumer and firm decisions

coursesExamined.name: Econometrics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
coursesExamined.contribution: Direct method contribution: OLS, GLS, instrumental variables, statistical tests and an empirical paper support causal and predictive analysis; applications are not restricted to business and the course uses Stata.

coursesExamined.name: Consumer Product Design
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Teaches consumer-product design and development through projects that progress from understanding an existing product to creating a new one. Students investigate product mechanisms and environmental impact, interview potential customers, translate needs into specifications, select concepts, and develop production plans and prototypes where feasible. The final project integrates these stages with industrial scaling and elementary economic analysis. Sustainability, including material use, repairability, lifespan and circularity, informs design decisions throughout.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops product innovation through customer needs, design, costing and team development

coursesExamined.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Connects marketing strategy and consumer psychology to responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students study strategic planning, customer experience, qualitative and quantitative insights, brand identity, digital marketing and behavioural framing. Applied projects analyze a company's strategy and response to disruption, design a brand, and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Customer-journey mapping translates findings into recommendations.
coursesExamined.contribution: examines marketing strategy, consumer psychology and responsible customer engagement

coursesExamined.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops business strategy from vision to execution and responsible digital transformation

traceOverrides.rationale: Business strategy from vision to execution places quantitative and financial decisions within organisational goals; digital transformation is one setting.

coursesExamined.name: Market Research
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas. Ready to turn curiosity into career skills? Perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops applied business research through data gathering, analysis and managerial recommendations

coursesExamined.name: International Business & Governance
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines how international trade, globalization and political, sociocultural and technological forces shape firms' cross-border decisions. Economic foundations include trade theories, foreign direct investment, foreign exchange and the monetary system. Students analyze governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate an international-business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy covering country attractiveness and business functions. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices and negotiation.
coursesExamined.contribution: examines institutions, culture, governance and corporate responsibility in global business

traceOverrides.rationale: Institutions, culture, governance and corporate responsibility situate international business and financial decisions.

coursesExamined.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions through the development of a startup concept. Students use design thinking to discover customer needs, define a problem, generate and prototype solutions, and construct value propositions and business models. Marketing, finance, operations, human resources and funding inform a coherent business plan and investor pitch. Entrepreneurial cases and a startup simulation examine decision-making, early growth and business lifecycles, with attention to societal impact and sustainability.
coursesExamined.contribution: Specific complementary contribution: teamwork, market validation and venture planning apply business strategy and innovation to a new business.

coursesExamined.name: Research Methods & Statistics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides research design, surveys, experiments and statistical analysis for management questions

coursesExamined.name: Personal Leadership
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces leadership through self-leadership, leadership theory and emotional intelligence. Covey's habits provide a framework for personal vision, prioritization and collaboration, alongside transformational, authentic, situational and adaptive leadership perspectives. Students analyze personality and emotional-intelligence profiles in relation to group dynamics, examine leadership cases, and construct a personal development plan with actionable goals. Assessment tools support educational reflection rather than diagnosis, and the outline acknowledges differences in their scientific support.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops leadership theory, self-awareness and applied leadership practice

coursesExamined.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, emotional expression and suppression, emotional labor, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership and social interaction under conflict, exclusion and interpersonal uncertainty. It emphasises inclusive leadership and ethnic, cultural, sexual and gender minority experiences, with digital emotion regulation as a further strand. Students conduct a supervised quantitative survey project: formulating theory-driven hypotheses, selecting established psychological measures, designing and piloting a Qualtrics survey, recruiting participants ethically, collecting original data and preparing a clean dataset. Individual work applies descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression in SPSS or RStudio, and interprets findings and limitations in empirical reports and evidence-based leadership recommendations.
coursesExamined.contribution: Emotion regulation, emotional labour, belonging, identity, psychological safety and inclusive leadership provide specific workforce psychology. An ethical supervised survey connects measurement, reliability and regression with leadership recommendations; it does not cover full human-resource management.

coursesExamined.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines organizational behaviour at individual, group and organizational levels. Topics connect personality, perception, emotions and motivation to teams, leadership, power, conflict, structure, culture and change. Students design research plans for organizational cases and conduct a brief systematic literature review using PRISMA reporting tools. Workshops develop literature searching, study selection, source appraisal and synthesis, linking organizational-psychology evidence to practical questions and recommendations.
coursesExamined.contribution: examines motivation, groups, organisational culture and structures through organisational psychology

coursesExamined.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops negotiation as an analytical practice and interpersonal skill. Students learn interest-based bargaining, BATNA and ZOPA, value creation, framing, concessions and strategies for handling power, emotions and difficult counterparts. Social-psychological and communication perspectives connect negotiation to trust, ethics, culture and relationships. Frequent simulations and narrative analysis lead to an annotated negotiation film and the design, teaching and evaluation of a negotiation scenario grounded in Delta Climate Center themes.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops negotiation, strategic interaction and analytical decision-making

coursesExamined.name: AI Ethics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines AI through ethical theory and psychological accounts of human behaviour and interaction. Ethical debates address fairness, privacy, responsibility, alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Psychological perspectives consider development, clinical care, social and organizational relationships, forensic applications and cognitive neuroscience. Students synthesize literature and apply ethical frameworks in an analytical psychology project and a research-grounded podcast, with a creative communication component.
coursesExamined.contribution: examines ethical and societal questions raised by artificial intelligence

coursesExamined.name: Database Management Systems
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces relational database management systems and SQL. Covers relational database theory, authorization, normalization and query processing.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides relational database and SQL skills for structured organisational information

coursesExamined.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies algorithm design and analysis, emphasizing how algorithms and data structures affect execution time. Students examine sorting, searching, random-number generation, string matching and graph algorithms, then study computability, verification, reductions and complexity classes. Programming and mathematical exercises develop algorithmic understanding, while projects require students to design, execute and report experimental investigations of performance.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops algorithmic problem-solving and data structures needed for computational business applications

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Data Science
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data. Students import, clean, transform and join data, explore patterns, and construct visualizations using tidy-data principles and the grammar of graphics. Web scraping and basic programming functions extend the workflow. A student research project applies these tools to a question using data from a field of interest.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops data cleaning, visualisation and manipulation for evidence-based business analysis

traceOverrides.rationale: Data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation support empirical economic and business analysis.

coursesExamined.name: Machine Learning
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes. Students study regression and classification, model accuracy, resampling, regularization, nonlinear models, trees, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Practical assignments evaluate methods on real data using R or Python. Projects emphasize informative predictor construction, test-set prediction, appropriate model choice and clear reporting of results and limitations.
coursesExamined.contribution: introduces machine-learning models for prediction and analysis of real datasets

traceOverrides.rationale: introduces machine-learning models for evidence-based analysis within the programme's data and technology strand
Machine-learning models and evaluation support prediction under uncertainty; their actual datasets need not concern finance.

coursesExamined.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops neural-network theory and practical implementation in Python, Keras and TensorFlow. Students build and train simple networks before studying multilayer architectures, backpropagation, regularization and model evaluation. Later work applies deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects construct predictors for tabular data and investigate an independently chosen image- or text-based prediction problem, with experimental results reported in a paper.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops neural-network and deep-learning methods for advanced AI applications

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Programming
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces computational problem-solving and programming in Python. Students develop structured programs using branching, iteration, functions and data collections, then progress to recursion, exception handling and object-oriented programming with inheritance. Elements of logic, sets and enumeration support computational reasoning. Exercises and projects require students to write, trace, test, debug and explain programs that solve problems of moderate complexity.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides programming foundations for computational and AI-oriented business work

traceOverrides.rationale: Programming foundations implement reproducible computational analysis for quantitative decisions; no finance-specific assignment is assumed.

coursesExamined.name: Mathematical Methods
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops single-variable calculus and related mathematical tools for modelling scientific problems. Functions, limits and differentiation lead to optimization, Taylor series, complex numbers, integration and differential equations. Students solve problems analytically and with Mathematica, including numerical approximation. A project implements, analyzes and adapts a dynamic model, requiring interpretation of its behaviour and explanation of the computational results.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides mathematical foundations for quantitative and data-driven modelling

traceOverrides.rationale: Mathematical foundations support the linear algebra, numerical methods, probability and optimisation used in this programme.

coursesExamined.name: Linear Algebra
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops linear algebra from systems of equations and matrix operations to vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and orthogonality. Students study least-squares approximation, symmetric matrices, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis. Mathematica exercises teach computer-algebra approaches to larger problems alongside analytical problem-solving.
coursesExamined.contribution: Specific complementary foundation: matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations support the quantitative modelling used by the AI strand.

traceOverrides.rationale: Matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations support statistical models, numerical computation and optimisation.

coursesExamined.name: Probability & Statistics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Provides a rigorous introduction to probability and mathematical statistics, from probability spaces and random variables to multivariate distributions and statistical inference. Students study estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and maximum-likelihood methods, followed by an introduction to Bayesian reasoning. Mathematica simulations verify analytical results. A substantial project implements and compares random-sampling algorithms, including inverse sampling, accept-reject sampling and Gibbs sampling.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides probability, statistical inference and simulation foundations for risk and analytics

coursesExamined.name: Social Psychology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces the scientific study of how thoughts, feelings and behaviour are shaped by other people and social situations. Social cognition, the self, influence and persuasion lead into group processes, prejudice, aggression, prosocial behaviour, attraction and close relationships. Students critically examine empirical research, synthesize findings from journal articles, formulate theory-guided questions and design a feasible study. The final project proposes research rather than conducting an empirical investigation.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides scientific analysis of social influence, group behaviour and interpersonal processes relevant to organisations and customers

coursesExamined.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Teaches rhetorical analysis and persuasive communication through classical history, theory and practice. Students study Greek and Roman rhetoric, the five canons, types of discourse, persuasive appeals, argumentation and fallacies. Written exercises, debates and public speeches develop invention, arrangement, style, memory and delivery. An applied project creates narrative and storytelling material for an immersive educational setting concerned with Zeeland's climate and community.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops persuasive written and spoken communication for organisational and stakeholder contexts

coursesExamined.name: Public Economics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines government intervention through the efficiency and equity effects of public policy. Market failure, public goods and externalities provide foundations for studying public production, collective choice, spending and taxation. Health, education, welfare and social insurance illustrate expenditure and redistribution questions. Students apply economic models, interpret data and graphs, evaluate research and develop a research proposal and paper.
coursesExamined.contribution: Market failure, public spending, tax incidence, efficiency, equity and collective choice situate economic and financial decisions within public policy. This is a complementary institutional contribution, not corporate tax law.

coursesExamined.name: Behavioral Economics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.
coursesExamined.contribution: Biases, heuristics, framing and experiments explain economic and financial decisions through behavioural theory. No dedicated investment experiment is assumed.

coursesExamined.name: Decision-making in AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops the mathematical foundations of intelligent-agent decisions under uncertainty. Probability and Bayesian networks support belief updating and inference, while temporal models address changing environments. Decision theory, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems connect uncertainty to policies and expected utility. Multi-agent decisions introduce strategic and collective interaction, and probabilistic programming provides a framework for expressing models. Students work through equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.
coursesExamined.contribution: Probabilistic inference, expected utility, Markov and partially observable decisions, bandits and multiagent choices supply rigorous methods for decisions under uncertainty. Their contribution is methodological; a trading application is not assumed.

coursesExamined.name: Optimization Methods in AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies search and optimization for rational agents in known, complex and adversarial environments. Students move from uninformed and heuristic search to local and global optimization, first- and second-order methods and population approaches. Adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimization extend the toolkit. Laboratories and projects require algorithm tracing, implementation and evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.
coursesExamined.contribution: Optimisation, linear programming, constraints and search supply decision-support methods also relevant to IBA methods training. Actual course projects are algorithmic; corporate-finance applications are not assumed.

coursesExamined.name: Advanced Algorithms
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies algebraic algorithms and advanced optimization methods through mathematical reasoning, implementation and experimental analysis. Fast and exact arithmetic, number-theoretic algorithms, matrix multiplication and Fourier transformation lead into hashing, greedy methods, dynamic programming and network flows. Laboratories develop algorithmic understanding, while projects investigate exact computing and optimization, including hypotheses, measured performance and sensitivity analysis.
coursesExamined.contribution: Dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, network flows and optimisation, with performance and sensitivity experiments, support computational decision analysis. These methods complement financial theory rather than supplying it.

coursesExamined.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops numerical solutions to mathematical problems that lack convenient analytical solutions, emphasizing when algorithms work and how to validate their output. Students study numerical root finding, interpolation, differentiation, quadrature, ordinary differential equations, and linear and nonlinear systems. Mathematica notebooks apply and compare textbook algorithms with built-in routines, with attention to roundoff, convergence, error, stability and sensitivity.
coursesExamined.contribution: Numerical root finding, quadrature, differential equations and linear and nonlinear systems, with error and stability checks, implement the quantitative modelling priority. No finance-specific project is assumed.

coursesExamined.name: Ethics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading. Utilitarianism, consequentialism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics lead into Nietzsche's genealogy, Murdoch's account of goodness and Nagel's treatments of value, perspective, death and meaning. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.
coursesExamined.contribution: Ethical theories, argument evaluation and practical moral problems support responsible assessment of financial and business decisions. This is a complementary normative contribution, not a professional accounting-ethics course.

academicJudgment: The actual BENBUSI112 profile includes financial and management accounting, costing, budgeting, control and discounted cash-flow appraisal. BENBUSI312 covers securities, financial markets, banking, regulation and risk, including a bank simulation with forecasts and capital/liquidity decisions. These substantive contributions overturn the narrow earlier rejection. Economics and econometrics connect institutions and behaviour with numerical methods, statistical inference, uncertainty and optimisation. International strategy, public policy and moral reasoning give these methods a concrete setting. The third option is a related financial-markets and quantitative-decisions programme, with explicit international-accounting and tax gaps. It does not promise finance-specific assignments in technical courses.
descriptionOnly: Market Research, Strategy and Digital Transformation, Econometrics, Database Management and Behavioral Economics receive full consideration within their actual descriptions. No unavailable outline or assignment is invented. Quantitative decision courses are assessed through actual probabilistic and optimisation methods.
alignmentFinding: All 38 external components and 39 UCR row identities were reviewed. Fifteen specific partial relationships remain; 23 gaps remain blank. Actual regression in Methods Master Classes supports the econometrics relationship. Accounting is the strongest foundational accounting relationship, without automatic repetition against management accounting or corporate finance. Finance, workforce psychology and technology-management claims were narrowed. Optional independent research is 15 EC once per UCR alternative beside the required 7-EC project, outside the 24-course/180-EC programme.
qualitativeDistinctness: The broad programme prioritises cross-border functions, people, marketing, law and management. The AI route shifts priorities toward programming, data and neural networks. The third prioritises economic and financial institutions and rigorous quantitative decisions. The pairs differ by 8, 11 and 10 courses (60, 82.5 and 75 EC respectively).
